build.#: The zena command: the host binary and the CLI module it runs.

build:bundle.#: The binary with out/zena.wasm and the standard library embedded. Split the way build:host is, and for the same reasons.

build:bundle:cargo.#: Recompiles zena-cli to embed out/zena.wasm and stdlib into the host binary once built.

build:bundle-assets.#: Generates out/stdlib_bundle.rs from stdlib sources and out/zena.wasm via bundle.zena.

build:host.#: Two scripts for one build. `build:host:cargo` declares no inputs, so wireit never calls it fresh and cargo is always consulted — cargo tracks its own inputs better than a `files` list could, and a no-op is a quarter of a second. This one names the binary cargo produced as an *input*, so its fingerprint changes exactly when the binary does, and that is what dependents inherit. `cascade: false` keeps `build:host:cargo`'s own fingerprint out: a script with no `files` is not `fullyTracked`, and wireit propagates that to everything downstream, where nothing can ever be fresh — which is why one `npm test` with no changes used to rebuild the whole bootstrap chain. Hashing the binary also makes freshness imply the binary exists, so the exit-127 case that a `files` list alone would have allowed cannot happen.

build:host:cargo.#: Always runs; `build:host` is what dependents read. See its comment.

build:module.#command: The compiler just built from source compiles the CLI module, run on zena-run with the preopens `zc` expects. It keeps its name section, like the compiler, so a trap in it names functions. The module then precompiles itself, so the first zena commands do not race to run Cranelift on it.
build:module.command: mkdir -p out && cd ../.. && ZENA_GC_RESERVE_MB=1536 ZENA_DEBUG_NAMES=1 ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. --dir packages/stdlib/zena::/stdlib packages/zena-compiler/zena/out/cli.wasm packages/zena-cli/zena/main.zena -o packages/zena-cli/out/zena.wasm && ./target/release/zena-cli precompile packages/zena-cli/out/zena.wasm

test.#command: --release reuses the dependency artifacts the build step produced instead of compiling wasmtime a second time in the dev profile.
